newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba - serious efforts to reach revaluation deal.
newsitem.headline: Buba - serious efforts to reach revaluation deal.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Wednesday that it and the German finance ministry were making serious efforts to reach an agreement on the revaluation of certain assets in the bank's 1997 balance sheet which would lead to a payout in 1998.

A Bundesbank spokesman said that the bank and the finance ministry were holding talks aimed at formulating a draft law to that effect which would be passed on to a parliamentary committee for discussion.
The spokesman reiterated Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer's statement on Tuesday night that no formal agreement had been reached yet but that the two sides were close to an agreement.
The spokesman read out the following statement:
"Finance Minister Theo Waigel and Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer on June 3 held talks on envisaged changes to the Bundesbank balance sheet.
"There are serious efforts to reach an agreement on a revaluation of certain items in 1997 with payment effect in 1998.

"The finance ministry and the Bundesbank are holding talks on the formulation of draft legislation. Finally the results will be submitted to the parliamentary committee stage of the Bundestag (lower house of the Federal Parliament)."
The spokesman made the statement to news agencies following erroneous media reports which had quoted Tietmeyer as denying that an agreement had been reached.

Tietmeyer told reporters in Interlaken, Switzerland on Tuesday night that no formal deal had yet been struck on Bonn's plans to revalue the central bank's official reserves but added that the two sides were close to an agreement.
